dimensions.name: past work
dimensions.evidence: Led a 5-person AI trip planner at KKday handling ~300k daily requests; personally wrote agent design, core backend, SSE stream reader, plan validation, personalization layer, and day-card rendering. Diagnosed a subtle ordering bug via logs and connection IDs, added regression tests, and monitored production drop logs. Also described a Debon Securities release risk with a feature switch, rollback plan, and post-release monitoring thresholds.

dimensions.name: current ability
dimensions.evidence: Designed a mobile wallet with clear client/server/local-storage ownership, idempotent transfers via client IDs, server-authoritative ledger, row locking plus conditional updates, unique index on client ID, same-transaction ledger and idempotency writes, and explicit handling of lost responses, process death, account switching, and concurrent sends. Explained trade-offs and failure modes with concrete tests.

dimensions.name: handling unknowns
dimensions.evidence: Clarified requirements before designing; handled ambiguous chat-initiated payments by requiring native confirmation and server-bound approval; addressed model-generated 'sent' messages as unconfirmed; covered reinstall, expired idempotency windows, not-found ambiguity, and late responses after navigation. Proposed backoff, retry caps, and reconciliation.

dimensions.name: shipping product
dimensions.evidence: Scoped a two-week MVP with balance, send, history, details, and pending/unknown states; defined sign-off with tech lead, product owner, and QA; listed pre-release failure tests; described a half-hour incident response with pause, reconciliation, clear ownership, escalation cap, and user-facing honesty.

strongest: Deep, production-grounded mobile and backend ownership: idempotent payment design, concurrency control, failure handling, and incident response all backed by concrete mechanisms, tests, and trade-offs.
risks: Some answers are very detailed and may over-index on edge cases; the two-week MVP scope and cross-team coordination could still be tight. The candidate's experience is strong but the interview did not probe people management or broader product strategy.
